mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above the 5-year monthly average precedes a short-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-year monthly average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 5-day moving average during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, reducing equity risk premia and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, average 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during prior high-UNRATE periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% are associated with higher S&P 500 5-day forward returns, reflecting stronger near-term demand for equities.
candidate_trigger: HOUST grows by ≥2% in a month
failure_condition: Over 50 such triggers, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 100 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During such contraction periods, 20-day forward returns do not fall as predicted (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the inflation surprise triggers a short-term negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: Over 10 such inflation spikes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in PAYEMS and UNRATE for two consecutive months suggest labor market softening, which amplifies equity risk aversion and drives negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat despite sustained labor weakening (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (GDP) by at least 2% for 4 consecutive months signals robust economic momentum, which is associated with positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by ≥2% monthly for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not outperform the prior 60-day average during such expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls for three consecutive months below its 12-month average, it indicates weak consumer demand, which is linked to negative S&P 20-day forward returns in the following two months.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month monthly average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during baseline periods (p > 0.05).
